title: Increased Bearing Land Thickness on the Outboard Flap Carriage Support Fittings

issue.reason: Original issue of the thickened carriage support bearing land dossier.

ata.title: Wing Trailing Edge — Flap Support Structure

abstract: Thicker bearing lands on the outboard flap carriage support fittings of the CIRRANE-13, answering a fretting finding at the carriage pin bore that shortened the fitting life below its design service goal.

sections.reason: Teardown of two outboard flap carriage support fittings returned from high-cycle CIRRANE-13 aircraft found fretting damage in the carriage pin bore that the original substantiation had not predicted. The measured wear rate projects a fitting life of about 42 000 flight cycles against a design service goal of 60 000. The CIRRANE-11 fitting sees a lower carriage load and is unaffected. No in-service failure has occurred and no operator has reported a symptom; the change is driven by the teardown evidence and the fleet's high cycle accumulation rate.
sections.description: The bearing land of the outboard flap carriage support lug, part number D5730124726204, is thickened by 4 mm on each face and the bore is given a hard anodised sleeve. The adjacent cleat BRDE298405-27 is replaced by a taller item so that the load path into the fixed trailing edge is unchanged, and the shear tie D5730118419315 is re-drilled to suit. The carriage locking mechanism, functional item number 8VU9, is not altered but its proximity target is repositioned by 4 mm to follow the fitting face. Revised detail is on drawings D57300006162 and D57300018013. Work is done from below in zones 561 and 661 with the flap in the fully extended position, and the trailing edge panel in zone 525 removed on the left-hand side only.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 5.2 kg per aircraft for the four fittings, symmetric about the centre line. No electrical load change. The fitting is not interchangeable with the previous standard because the cleat height and the shear tie drilling change together. The teardown-driven inspection introduced in 2023 for the pin bore is withdrawn once the modification is embodied. Flap rigging values are unchanged but the rigging task gains a target-position check. Illustrated parts and repair content for the flap support structure both need re-issue.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00655 in May 2024. Retrofit for delivered CIRRANE-13 aircraft is offered through Service Bulletin CRN-57-1006 and needs the flap to be removed, so it is scheduled with a flap track lubrication visit. Long lead item is the sleeved lug at thirty-eight weeks.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00655, wing equipping station resequenced by half a shift
